what_its_for: Ruxolitinib is used to treat certain blood disorders and inflammatory conditions. It is used for myelofibrosis (a bone marrow disorder), polycythemia vera (a condition where your body makes too many red blood cells), graft-versus-host disease (a complication after a bone marrow transplant), and as a cream for non-segmental vitiligo (a skin condition causing loss of skin color) and atopic dermatitis (eczema). It works by blocking certain proteins in your body that cause inflammation and abnormal cell growth.
how_to_take: For tablets: Swallow the tablet whole with or without food. Try to take it at the same times each day. If you have trouble swallowing the tablet, you may dissolve it in water and drink it right away. For cream (Opzelura): Apply a thin layer to the affected skin areas as directed by your doctor. Wash your hands before and after applying the cream. Do not get the cream in your eyes, mouth, or vagina.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition, lab results, and other medicines you take. Common starting doses for tablets range from 5 mg to 20 mg taken twice daily. The cream is usually applied twice daily. Never change your dose on your own — always follow your doctor's instructions exactly. Your dose may be adjusted over time based on how your body responds and your blood test results.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose of the tablet, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regularly scheduled time. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you miss a dose of the cream, apply it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next application, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule.
storage: Store tablets at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep them away from moisture, heat, and direct light. Store the cream at room temperature and do not freeze it. Keep all forms of this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush medications down the toilet unless the label says to do so.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice while taking ruxolitinib tablets, as it can increase the amount of medicine in your blood and cause more side effects. Avoid crowded places or people who are sick, because this medicine can lower your ability to fight infections. Do not start any new prescription or over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, or herbal supplements without asking your doctor or pharmacist first, as many medicines can interact with ruxolitinib. Avoid live vaccines (such as the nasal flu spray or shingles vaccine) while on this medication — talk to your doctor about which vaccines are safe. For the cream, avoid applying to broken or infected skin unless your doctor tells you to.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: signs of infection such as fever, chills, sore throat, or unusual cough; signs of bleeding such as unusual bruising, blood in your urine or stool, or prolonged bleeding from cuts; sudden severe headache, weakness, or numbness (possible signs of stroke); chest pain or shortness of breath; signs of low blood counts such as extreme tiredness or paleness; skin changes such as new growths, sores, or changes in moles; severe stomach pain; or if you feel faint or dizzy. Also tell your doctor if you develop any new skin cancer or if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant.
when_it_works: Many patients begin to notice improvement within a few weeks of starting treatment, but the full benefit may take several months. For myelofibrosis, you may notice that your spleen gets smaller and your symptoms such as night sweats, bone pain, and fatigue improve within 4 to 6 weeks. For vitiligo cream, it may take several months to see repigmentation of the skin. Do not stop taking this medicine on your own even if you feel better — stopping suddenly can cause your symptoms to return quickly and sometimes severely.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older): You may be more sensitive to the side effects of ruxolitinib. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose and monitor you more closely. Kidney or liver problems: Your dose may need to be adjusted. Make sure your doctor knows about any kidney or liver issues before starting this medicine. Pregnancy: Ruxolitinib can harm an unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least one week after stopping. Tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding: You should not breastfeed while taking ruxolitinib tablets or using the cream, as the medicine may pass into breast milk. Children: The tablets are approved for certain conditions in children 12 years and older. The cream (Opzelura) is approved for children 12 years and older for atopic dermatitis and vitiligo. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for pediatric use.
